email.body1:
Chad, saw Fiery just rolled out JobFlow Pro and Fiery Scribe, your agentic AI for print job submission.

Launching that many products usually means more in-market accounts than a sales development team can touch before interest fades, and that is where deals slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Fiery off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Chad, quick follow-up for Fiery.

When the product line expands, reps spend more time on research and CRM than on print shops that are ready to buy, so the best-fit accounts get a generic touch. Tightening emails to 75-100 words alone tends to lift responses about 67%, and most teams never hit that at scale.

I had our AI SDR draft 3 personalized emails to your top 3 target accounts. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through them?
email.body3:
Chad, last bit of proof for Fiery.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Fiery's reply rate likely compares to other production-software teams. Want to grab time so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Chad, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling outbound coverage without adding reps isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Right after a wave of launches, pipeline coverage rarely gets the attention it needs, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your sales development motion? I'll tailor it to Fiery either way.
